correctness.rationale: The finite Cayley graph on F_2^4 is explicitly defined. Translation and the S_5 symmetry of its five generators reduce all three-vertex placements to three induced-subgraph types and all 2K2 placements to one type. Direct neighborhood calculations with explicit forcing witnesses settle the canonical cases. An edge-count contradiction rules out larger failures. The 320 minimum triples and 60 maximal failed fours have combinatorial counts; both independent Python set and C++ bit-mask implementations exhaustively verified 65536 sensor sets, 240 unique triple extensions and 320 complete BFS profiles, each (1,21,126,172). The graph has 3360 exchange edges and diameter three. The executable verification files are included in this same package.

originality.rationale: The result is not the known power-domination definition, a standard hypercube bound, a zero-forcing polynomial, a conventional domination count, or a claim about an ordinary five-cube. Two closest directly relevant primary works were inspected in full and neither treats Clebsch placements or their optimal exchange geometry. Relevant prior exact Clebsch and power-domination claims were compared by implication and found not to subsume this full theorem. Residual unindexed-priority risk is stated.
residual_risks: Some earlier historical ledgers and unindexed unpublished computations were not available and could contain the same exact invariant.
The 2002 founding paper was inspected via scholarly abstract rather than full text; it is foundational and not used for a whole-document exclusion.
The exchange metric was checked by exhaustive reproducible finite code rather than an independent peer-reviewed proof; external validation remains unperformed.

value.rationale: This is a naturally complete failure classification for a canonical strongly regular triangle-free graph rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The induced-triple criterion, unique maximal failure completion of each bad triple, and exact 21-regular connected exchange graph of diameter three provide useful structural recognition and sensor-replacement properties that neither the scalar optimum nor an unrelated graph invariant supplies. An exact finite invariant is appropriate for this special highly symmetric host; an infinite-family generalization is not asserted.
